clue.text: Aristocrat getting half of tax on game

indicators.note: only the front half of a word for tax is kept, the first two of its four letters

parts.note: a duty is a tax on goods
chess is a board game

explanation.surface: A nobleman is taxed on the board game he plays.
explanation.definitionFit: A duchess is a noblewoman of high rank, the wife of a duke, so an aristocrat.

clue.text: Abolish one method to get humour into Homerian acknowledgement of stupidity

indicators.note: the pieces go into the exclamation, so that word is split open around them

parts.note: D'oh is Homer Simpson's catchphrase when he realises he has been stupid
one is the indefinite article a
a way of doing something is a method
wit is clever humour

explanation.surface: A recipe for getting a joke into Homer Simpson's exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Homerian' points to the cartoon character Homer Simpson, not the Greek poet.
explanation.definitionFit: To do away with something is to get rid of it entirely, the idiom for scrapping a law or practice.

clue.text: Church of Rome: six of its members shunned superficially shiny stuff

indicators.note: six of the phrase's letters, its members, are cast out: the run URCH OF from the middle

explanation.surface: A schism in the Catholic Church, with six members excommunicated for being shallow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six of its members shunned' removes six letters from the twelve of 'Church of Rome', leaving CH and ROME joined.
explanation.definitionFit: Chrome plating is a thin bright layer of metal, shiny only on the surface.

clue.text: It indicates the previous clue, say, is less sensitive than before

definitions.text: It indicates the previous clue, say
definitions.meaning: the clue before this one is 2, which is divisible by two

explanation.surface: A puzzle about how the clue before reads, and someone growing numb.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into EVEN (still more) and NUMBER (more numb).
explanation.definitionFit: Two is divisible by two, so the preceding clue number illustrates this; and 'even number' can mean still more lacking in feeling.

clue.text: School's head, useless creep

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: idle can mean pointless or ineffective, as in idle threats

explanation.surface: A headteacher dismissed as a worthless toady.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidle is to edge along furtively, much as one would creep.

clue.text: US fast food is old-fashioned stuff — make good

parts.note: corn is trite or sentimental material that seems dated
do can mean make, as in do a drawing

explanation.surface: A complaint that American fast food is dated and needs improving.
explanation.definitionFit: A corn dog is a sausage on a stick dipped in cornmeal batter and fried, an American fairground snack.

clue.text: Artisan's stylus possessed by renowned Egyptologist

indicators.note: the writing tool is held inside the archaeologist's surname

parts.note: Howard Carter discovered Tutankhamun's tomb
a stylus is a writing implement, like a pen

explanation.surface: An archaeologist owns a craftsman's writing tool.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'Artisan' stands for 'is', linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpenter is a skilled woodworker, one kind of craftsman.

clue.text: Upper class Henry entering bishop's address here in Germany

indicators.note: the two letters go into the form of address

parts.note: a bishop is styled Right Reverend, RR
U is the old shorthand for upper class
H is the symbol of the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A posh man called Henry visits a bishop's residence somewhere in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Address' suggests a home, but here it is the bishop's title, Right Reverend.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ruhr is the industrial region of western Germany, a place there.

clue.text: Animal used moor for recreation

indicators.note: re-creation, making again, signals the letters are remade into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A creature that played on the moorland.
explanation.definitionFit: A dormouse is a small hibernating rodent, so an animal.

clue.text: Ancient vessel — pull a nasty face, inhaling smoke

indicators.note: the face-pulling word breathes in the smoke word, holding it inside

parts.note: to gurn is to make a grotesque face
reek is an old and Scottish word for smoke

explanation.surface: Someone grimaces at an antique pot while breathing in smoke.
explanation.walkthrough: Gurning is a British contest of pulling ugly faces.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek urn is an ornate jar from classical antiquity, an old container.

clue.text: Greylag reed houses share a view

indicators.note: the two words house the answer, holding it in their letters across the gap

explanation.surface: Geese in the reeds seemingly in accord.
explanation.walkthrough: A greylag is a wild goose.
explanation.definitionFit: To agree is to be of the same opinion as someone, holding a common outlook.

clue.text: Hardly a revealing character, Black Beauty?

definitions.meaning: a person who keeps their talents or plans secret
Black Beauty is a famous fictional black horse; the question mark flags the example

explanation.surface: Musing on whether the famous fictional horse is secretive.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark horse is someone secretive with hidden abilities, and literally a horse of black colour, like Black Beauty.

clue.text: Deadly omen affected Tutankhamun, visually

indicators.note: affected means altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The pharaoh's curse, a fatal portent that struck Tutankhamun.
explanation.walkthrough: Recalls the legend of the curse of the tomb, but the definition describes the boy king's painted eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: Egyptian portraits of the king show elongated oval eyes, so in appearance he had that shape of eye.

clue.text: I'm astonished by Köchel's fiddle

parts.note: coo is an exclamation of surprise
K is the Köchel catalogue number prefix for Mozart's works

explanation.surface: Delight at a violin listed in the Mozart catalogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddle' looks like a violin, but it is the verb meaning falsify.
explanation.definitionFit: To cook the books is to fiddle them, falsifying accounts.

clue.text: One who makes longer drawing instrument

definitions.meaning: someone who protracts, dragging things out
a semicircular tool for measuring angles in technical drawing

explanation.surface: A device for drawing that stretches things out.
explanation.definitionFit: To protract is to prolong, so a protractor lengthens; it is also the geometry tool for measuring angles.

clue.text: Increase in tourism misrepresented, which is rather a dampener

indicators.note: the word for increase goes inside the rearranged letters
presented wrongly, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: a rise is an increase

explanation.surface: Spin about growth in tourism falls flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Misrepresented' rearranges the holiday-trade word to MOISTUR, and 'in' places the increase inside it; 'dampener' suggests spoiling the mood, but means something that wets.
explanation.definitionFit: A moisturising cream makes skin damp, so it is jokingly a dampener, though not one spoiling the mood.

clue.text: One medium Pils drunk without oxygen at the time of collapse

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
M is the abbreviation for medium, as in clothing sizes

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the jumbled letters surround the oxygen symbol
drunk means messed up, so the letters of the lager are rearranged

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
on can mean at the time of, as in on arrival

explanation.surface: A drinker downs a Pilsner with no air and falls over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' makes PLSI from PILS, and 'without' means outside: it goes round O to give PLOSI.
explanation.definitionFit: An implosion is a violent inward collapse, as of a vacuum tube.

clue.text: Cleaning up pop group not quite into rock

indicators.note: the shortened band name is placed inside the word for rock

parts.note: to rock is to swing back and forth

indicators.note: not quite the whole band name, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: Abba is the Swedish pop group

explanation.surface: A pop band nearly making it into rock music while tidying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' suggests music, but it means swing; 'not quite' trims ABBA to ABB.
explanation.definitionFit: Swabbing is mopping or wiping clean, as sailors do the deck.

clue.text: Bible's out with day, month, year for David or Jonathan?

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, and with gathers in the date letters to be mixed too

parts.note: the possessive ending is read as 'is', so only the book's name goes in
D and M are the abbreviations for day and month

explanation.surface: Biblical names David and Jonathan, with a calendar date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bible's' is Bible is; David and Jonathan suggest the biblical friends, but they are the British broadcasting brothers.
explanation.definitionFit: David and Jonathan are the well-known British broadcaster brothers of that surname; the question mark marks an example.

clue.text: Thinner, washed out, in need of courage

parts.note: white describes a pale, washed-out complexion
spirit means courage or mettle

explanation.surface: A slimmer person, pale and lacking nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thinner' looks like a comparative adjective, but it is the noun for a paint solvent.
explanation.definitionFit: White spirit is a petroleum solvent used to thin paint and clean brushes.

clue.text: Career time for hot shell-suited swimmer

indicators.note: one letter stands in for another, swapping the symbol for heat out

parts.note: to career is to rush headlong, to hurtle
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A dash in a shell suit, the shiny tracksuit, to go swimming.
explanation.walkthrough: A shell suit is a shiny nylon tracksuit, popular in Britain around 1990.
explanation.definitionFit: A turtle is a marine reptile encased in a hard shell, so a swimmer clad in one.

clue.text: Toothy creature happened to be holding back web address

indicators.note: the past tense verb holds the turned-round link inside it

parts.note: was is the past of be

indicators.note: back means the web address abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: a URL is the address of a web page

explanation.surface: A grinning animal that once kept a website address.
explanation.definitionFit: The walrus is an Arctic marine mammal with long tusks, so notably toothy.

clue.text: Dear little book found in stall

indicators.note: the book letter is found inside the word for a stall

parts.note: a bay is a compartment, such as a stall in a stable
B is the short form of book

explanation.surface: A sweet little book discovered on a market stand.
explanation.definitionFit: Baby is a term of endearment, used like darling or sweetheart.

clue.text: Decorative singer, actual or fraudulent, bags gold

indicators.note: bags means captures, so the scrambled letters hold the gold word inside
fraudulent means false, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A singer, whether real or fake, pockets the gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fraudulent' rearranges the first two words, and 'bags' holds the heraldic gold inside; 'or' does double duty in the surface as a mere conjunction.
explanation.definitionFit: A coloratura is a soprano specialising in elaborate ornamented runs and trills, so a singer of decoration.

clue.text: Anything at all should!

definitions.meaning: an old word for anything whatever, also spelt aught
a modal verb of duty, as in you should go

explanation.surface: An insistence that anything at all is obligatory.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is an archaic variant meaning anything, and the verb expresses obligation like should.

clue.text: See 1
I almost do casual work and I perform, making a list

indicators.note: almost the whole word, so its final letter is cut

parts.note: to temp is to do temporary jobs
to sing is to perform music

explanation.surface: Someone who temps and sings is drawing up an inventory.
explanation.definitionFit: Itemising is setting things out one by one, as entries in an itemised bill.

clue.text: Turning out in transitive school

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go inside the grammar abbreviation

parts.note: tr is the dictionary abbreviation for a transitive verb

indicators.note: turning means shifting around, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson on transitive verbs at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning' makes UTO from OUT; it is an anagram here, not a reversal, which would give TUO.
explanation.definitionFit: To school someone is to teach or coach them, which is what a private teacher does.

clue.text: Horny GP after surgery is a monster

indicators.note: surgery has rearranged the parts, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A lecherous family doctor turns out to be monstrous after the clinic.
explanation.walkthrough: A GP is a family doctor, and surgery is the British word for a doctor's consulting session.
explanation.definitionFit: A gryphon, or griffin, is a mythical beast with an eagle's head and a lion's body.

clue.text: Education basically ruined her rest

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Schooling spoiled her chance to relax.
explanation.definitionFit: Reading, writing and arithmetic are the fundamentals of schooling, the basics.
